entries.title: Not in an EAI project.
why: The current folder does not contain the project markers created by eai init.
The command needs a project root so it can read local app configuration safely.
You may be one directory above or below the generated app folder.
evidenceToCheck: Current working directory.
Whether package.json and src/eai.config/object-types.ts exist.
Whether eai verify reports the same project-root issue.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the current folder before changing anything.
Check whether the current folder is an EAI project.
If this is an EAI project, inspect template drift without writing files.

fixes.purpose: Move into a folder that has already been initialized.
Create a new EAI app project when this folder should become one.

stopWhen: The folder still has no EAI project markers after eai init or changing directory.

neededWhen: A freshly generated project still cannot be detected as an EAI project.

entries.title: Not logged in.
why: The CLI does not have a usable local sign-in token.
The token may have expired or been created for a different local profile.
The command needs a user session before it can resolve tenant access.
evidenceToCheck: eai whoami status.
Active profile, if a local profile is selected.
Whether the command is running on a machine or Codespace that has completed browser sign-in.

diagnostics.purpose: Show the current login and active tenant status.
Confirm tenant memberships after login succeeds.

fixes.purpose: Authenticate with the EAI identity flow.
Use a fixed local callback port for Codespaces or locked-down environments.
fixes.when: Use when the browser callback cannot reach the CLI.

stopWhen: The browser sign-in flow repeatedly fails with the same identity error.

neededWhen: Login succeeds but no expected tenant membership is visible.

entries.title: Access token expired.
why: The saved user session is older than the identity provider allows.
The CLI cannot refresh the session silently in this environment.
The command needs a fresh user token before it can call tenant-scoped APIs.
evidenceToCheck: eai whoami token status.
Whether the active profile changed since the last login.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the expired session and active profile.

fixes.purpose: Refresh the local user session.

stopWhen: A fresh login still returns an expired-token result.

neededWhen: A newly completed login immediately reports an expired token.
include: token expiry time without token values

entries.title: Permission denied.
why: The signed-in user can authenticate, but does not have the role required for this action.
The active tenant may not be the tenant where the user has the needed role.
The app or resource may require a tenant-admin or builder-level action.
evidenceToCheck: Active tenant in eai whoami.
Roles returned by eai tenant list --all --format json.
The exact command and request ID, if the server returned one.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the signed-in user and active tenant.
List visible tenant memberships and roles.

fixes.purpose: Switch to a tenant where the user has the required role.
Add or refresh a user membership and assign a tenant role when you are already tenant-admin for that tenant.
fixes.when: Use for normal "add this person as a tenant member/admin" requests.

fixes.purpose: List assignable tenant roles before choosing a role for an invite.
Repair first tenant-admin access for an immediate child tenant.
fixes.when: Only when the target tenant is an immediate child of the supplied parent and does not already have usable tenant-admin access.

stopWhen: The user lacks the required tenant role. Retrying will not change authorization.

neededWhen: No visible tenant membership has the role required by the command.

entries.title: The supplied tenant is not an immediate child of the supplied parent.
why: The child-tenant bootstrap command is intentionally narrow.
It only works when the parent ID is the direct parent of the child tenant.
This error often appears when an agent uses bootstrap-admin for normal user addition instead of the tenant member invite flow.
evidenceToCheck: Whether the task is normal user addition or first-admin child tenant repair.
The active tenant shown by eai whoami.
The target tenant shown by eai tenant info <tenant-id>.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the signed-in user and active tenant.
Inspect the target tenant before retrying a tenant relationship command.
List assignable roles when the intended task is adding or updating a user.

fixes.purpose: Add or update a user as tenant-admin on an existing tenant.
fixes.when: Use when the goal is to add a person to a tenant or app context.

fixes.purpose: Retry the child bootstrap repair with the direct parent and immediate child IDs.
fixes.when: Use only for first-admin child tenant repair, not normal member management.

stopWhen: The supplied parent and child are not a direct parent-child pair.

neededWhen: The direct parent tenant is not visible to the signed-in user.

entries.title: Tenant member invite failed, but an existing member role repair may be available.
why: The invite/add flow reached an external identity or notification dependency that returned a server-side failure.
The target person may already exist as a direct tenant member with a lower role, so retrying the same invite can fail without changing access.
When a member record already exists, the supported recovery is to update that member through EAI CLI instead of editing data stores or cloud portals directly.
Applications may cache tenant role claims in their Auth.js session or JWT, so the user may need to sign out and sign back in after a role change.
evidenceToCheck: HTTP status, server code, and request ID from the failed invite/add command.
Active tenant and profile from eai whoami.
Assignable roles from eai user roles --tenant <tenant-id> --format json.
Existing member record from eai user list --tenant <tenant-id> --search <email> --format json.
Read-back role after any eai user role set command.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the signed-in user, active tenant, and profile before changing membership.
Confirm the target role is assignable in this tenant.
Check whether the person already exists as a direct tenant member and capture the member ID.

fixes.command: eai user role set --tenant <tenant-id> --member-id <member-id> --role tenant-admin --format json
fixes.purpose: Update the existing direct member to tenant-admin through the approved EAI tenant-member role endpoint.
fixes.when: Use only after eai user list confirms the existing member ID and the user approves the role change.

fixes.purpose: Retry the normal invite/add flow when no existing direct member is found and the failure was transient.
fixes.when: Use only within the retry limit and after read-only diagnostics confirm the tenant and role.

stopWhen: The same external service error repeats after bounded retry.
The existing member is found but role update is not approved by the user.
The signed-in user is not allowed to change tenant membership.

neededWhen: No existing direct member is found and the invite/add flow keeps returning a 5xx or EXTERNAL_SERVICE_ERROR.

entries.title: App-token platform user lookup is missing tenant context.
why: The platform call authenticated, but the request did not carry the tenant context required for app-token user or membership operations.
This is commonly seen as MISSING_TENANT or "Tenant context required for app tokens" on platform user lookup or membership prerequisite calls.
Do not treat this as the first signal to edit tenant members, role definitions, Entra configuration, databases, or cloud portals.
For platform automation app-token flows outside tenant app runtime, use the tenant-scoped platform routes instead of root user lookup routes.
If the same route works in current main but fails in an environment, the deployed PublicAPI/AdminAPI may be behind the release that adds tenant-scoped routing hardening.
evidenceToCheck: The failed path and whether it is a root platform user route such as /v4/platform/users/by-email or /v4/platform/users/{oid}/memberships.
Whether the caller is using an app token rather than an end-user identity route.
Active tenant from eai whoami and eai tenant list --format json.
PublicAPI/AdminAPI deployed versions when the failure happens in a shared environment.
Whether a tenant-scoped path succeeds for the same operation.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm login, active tenant, profile, and PublicAPI context.
Confirm the target tenant is visible before retrying tenant-scoped calls.
Verify user lookup through the tenant-scoped platform route.
Verify membership lookup through the tenant-scoped platform route.

fixes.purpose: Select the tenant that should provide app-token context.
Replace root platform user lookup with the tenant-scoped V4 route in platform automation app-token flows.
Replace root platform membership lookup with the tenant-scoped V4 route in platform automation app-token flows.
Keep tenant member and role-definition reads on the tenant-scoped V4 surface.

stopWhen: The tenant-scoped route returns the same MISSING_TENANT result.
The environment is running older PublicAPI/AdminAPI versions than the release with tenant-scoped platform routing hardening.

neededWhen: Tenant-scoped routes still return MISSING_TENANT after confirming the tenant and current deployed versions.
Production or another shared environment is behind the release that contains tenant-scoped platform routing hardening.

entries.title: The application making this request is not authorized for the tenant.
why: The authorization decision applies to the client ID in the current CLI token.
It does not evaluate a different tenant app client, even when provision-me was run while diagnosing that app.
If the current user already has direct membership, provisioning is unnecessary.
evidenceToCheck: callingApplication.clientId in the structured error.
eai whoami active tenant and direct membership.
The intended app client from eai app auth status when diagnosing another app.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the current CLI identity, active tenant, and calling client context.
Inspect a different app client without changing tenant authorization.

fixes.command: Ask platform support to authorize the reported calling CLI client only if provision-me is required
fixes.purpose: Repair the caller-specific authorization without changing the target app or creating credentials.

stopWhen: Authorization state has not changed.

neededWhen: Direct membership is absent and the reported calling CLI client must perform user provisioning.

entries.title: Tenant data-plane authorization incomplete.
why: The app registration exists, but the selected tenant has not completed app authorization.
The active tenant may not be the tenant this app was provisioned for.
The authorization retry may need to run again after sign-in wiring is refreshed.
evidenceToCheck: eai whoami active tenant.
eai provision entra --force --debug tenant authorization summary.
Request ID and platform status if debug output includes one.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm login, active tenant, profile, and public API context.
Confirm the intended tenant is visible to the user.

fixes.purpose: Select the tenant that should own the app.
Refresh sign-in wiring and retry app authorization for the active tenant.
Create or refresh the current user membership after app authorization succeeds.
fixes.when: Run only after provision entra no longer reports incomplete tenant authorization.

stopWhen: The same platform 5xx or authorization status remains after bounded retry.

neededWhen: The platform authorization step continues to fail after bounded retry.

entries.title: Tenant app authorization could not be completed because the platform returned a server error.
why: The CLI tried to authorize the app for the selected tenant, but the platform returned a server-side failure.
This is usually not fixed by changing local files or repeatedly rotating app credentials.
The safest next step is a bounded retry followed by escalation with the request evidence.
evidenceToCheck: HTTP status from eai provision entra --force --debug.
Request ID if present.
Whether the same status repeats after bounded retry.

diagnostics.purpose: Retry once with product-safe diagnostics and request identifiers.
Confirm the active tenant and profile are still correct.

stopWhen: The same 5xx status repeats after bounded retry.

neededWhen: A platform 5xx repeats for the same authorization command.

entries.title: Tenant plan does not allow this builder operation.
why: The tenant is reachable, but the requested builder operation is gated by the tenant plan.
The CLI cannot self-upgrade a tenant plan.
Read-only checks may still work while write/build actions are blocked.
evidenceToCheck: Workflow readiness status and reason code.
Tenant active status from eai whoami.
Which command attempted a builder write.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm whether builder operations are available for the active tenant.
Confirm the active tenant before asking an admin to change plan state.

stopWhen: The readiness reason is paid_upgrade_required. Retrying does not activate the tenant plan.

neededWhen: A builder operation is required and readiness reports paid_upgrade_required.

entries.title: Object Type validation failed.
why: At least one local Object Type definition does not match the schema rules enforced by the CLI or platform.
Common causes include invalid default values, incomplete storage metadata, or missing required fields.
Publishing cannot continue until the local definitions validate.
evidenceToCheck: Validation details printed by eai types validate.
Object Type name and property path in the error output.
Whether the Object Type is marked published before storage metadata is ready.

diagnostics.purpose: Validate local Object Types without publishing them.
Compare local definitions with published tenant state after validation passes.

fixes.purpose: Publish the corrected definitions after validation passes.
fixes.when: Run only after eai types validate is clean.

stopWhen: The same validation issue is reported. Fix the local Object Type definition before retrying.

neededWhen: The definition appears valid but the CLI still rejects it.

entries.title: Object Type is not published for the active tenant.
why: The resource command is asking for a type that is not available in the active tenant schema.
The local Object Types may not have been published yet.
The active tenant may not be the tenant where the Object Type was published.
evidenceToCheck: Published type list from eai resources schema.
Active tenant from eai whoami.
Local Object Type definitions from eai types validate.

diagnostics.purpose: List published Object Types visible to the active tenant.
Check local definitions before publishing.

fixes.purpose: Publish local Object Types to the active tenant.
Switch to the tenant where the Object Type was published.
fixes.when: Use when the active tenant is wrong.

stopWhen: The type is still absent from eai resources schema after publishing and schema propagation.

neededWhen: types seed reports convergence but resources schema never shows the Object Type.

entries.title: Semantic resource search is not ready for this tenant.
why: The v4 resource search endpoint can be available for full-text search while semantic search modes are still not ready.
Hybrid and vector search need an additional semantic-search capability before the platform can create query embeddings.
This is not fixed by retrying the same hybrid or vector search command; use full-text search or check readiness first.
This guidance applies to eai resources commands using the public v4 resource surface.
evidenceToCheck: Search capabilities from eai resources storage doctor.
Whether the failed command used --hybrid, --vector, or the default hybrid mode.
Published Object Types from eai resources schema.

diagnostics.purpose: Check whether fulltext, hybrid, and vector search are ready for the active tenant.
Confirm the tenant has published Object Types to search.

fixes.purpose: Run a full-text search path that does not require semantic-search readiness.
fixes.when: Use this when storage doctor reports fulltext ready but hybrid/vector unavailable.

stopWhen: The same hybrid or vector command still reports semantic-search readiness as unavailable.
Full-text search also fails, which means the issue is broader than semantic-search readiness.

neededWhen: The app requires hybrid or vector search and storage doctor keeps reporting those modes unavailable.

entries.title: The PublicAPI v4 resource mutation contract is invalid.
why: PublicAPI v4 intentionally rejects legacy flat resource bodies and PATCH updates.
Create requires POST with {"data": {...}}.
Update requires PUT with {"data": {...}, "version": n}, where n is the latest resource version.
A resource action requires POST with {"params": {...}} and returns the new version for any follow-up update.
evidenceToCheck: The HTTP method and path used by the failed request.
The server error code and expected contract in the response.
The latest resource version when an update follows another mutation or action.

diagnostics.purpose: Read the current resource and version before an update.
diagnostics.when: Required for updates, especially after an action or another writer.

fixes.purpose: Create a resource using the strict v4 data envelope.
Update a resource with PUT and the latest optimistic-lock version.
Execute a resource action with the strict params envelope.

stopWhen: The corrected method and body still return the same contract error.
The update uses the latest version but returns a version conflict.

neededWhen: A request matching the documented strict v4 method and envelope is still rejected.

entries.title: Workflow runtime binding requires operator assistance.
why: The tenant and workflow key are recognized, but an executable runtime binding is not available yet.
Some workflow bindings require an operator-assisted request before chat or workflow execution can run.
The CLI should request the binding only when readiness reports operator_required.
evidenceToCheck: workflow readiness status and reason code.
workflow status for the specific workflow key.
request ID returned by eai workflow request.

diagnostics.purpose: Check tenant, plan, and workflow readiness.
Check whether the workflow has an executable runtime binding.

fixes.purpose: Request operator-assisted runtime binding for this tenant and workflow.
fixes.when: Run only when readiness or status reports operator_required.

stopWhen: A workflow request is already queued or the status remains operator_required.

neededWhen: The workflow request is queued but does not progress.

entries.title: Tenant data/schema setup is not fully provisioned.
why: The platform could not resolve an active data/schema install for this tenant.
This is a tenant setup issue, not a transient outage: the data/schema capability is reachable but has no active install registered for this tenant.
Object Type publish (eai types seed) and schema reads cannot complete until the tenant setup is completed. Retrying does not create that setup.
evidenceToCheck: The reason code in the response body.
Active tenant from eai whoami — confirm you are on the intended tenant.
Whether the same tenant also fails the data/schema check in eai verify.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the active tenant that failed to resolve a data/schema install.
Confirm whether the data/schema service can resolve an install for this tenant.

stopWhen: The response indicates no active tenant data/schema install. Retrying does not provision the tenant setup — it must be fixed by platform support.

neededWhen: A tenant cannot resolve an active data/schema install on publish or schema reads.
include: active tenant slug and id (eai whoami)
the request id from the error
the reason code from the error response
